```
74	 * - If no persisted settings → use "last used" (prompt = '')

77	 * - All changes save to generation

80	export function useEditSettingsPersistence({

106	  // Render-time reset: sanctioned React pattern for "adjust state during render based on
107	  // changed props". Safe because it only mutates refs + calls own setState (which React
108	  // batches). This must NOT be an effect — an effect would leave a render with stale
109	  // hasInitializedRef causing a flash of wrong settings.
110	  if (generationId !== lastGenerationIdRef.current) {

112	    lastGenerationIdRef.current = generationId;
113	    if (isReady) setIsReady(false);
114	  }

116	  // Effect-based init: must be an effect (not render-time) because initializeFromLastUsed

123	        initializeFromLastUsed(lastUsed);
124	        setIsReady(true);
125	      } else if (hasPersistedSettings) {
126	        hasInitializedRef.current = true;
127	        setIsReady(true);
128	      }

144	    if (generationSettings.hasPersistedSettings) {
```

```
121	async function saveGenerationSettings(generationId: string, settings: AutoSaveGenerationEditSettings): Promise<void> {
122	  // Fetch current params to merge
123	  const { data: current, error: fetchError } = await supabase().from('generations')
124	    .select('params')
125	    .eq('id', generationId)
126	    .maybeSingle();
127	
128	  if (fetchError) {
129	    throw new Error(`Failed to fetch current params: ${fetchError.message}`);
130	  }
131	
132	  if (!current) {
133	    // Generation was deleted, skip save
134	    return;
135	  }
136	
137	  // Merge with existing params
138	  const currentParams = ((current?.params as JsonObject | null) ?? {});
139	  const currentUi = ((currentParams.ui as JsonObject | undefined) ?? {});
140	  const updatedParams: JsonObject = {
141	    ...currentParams,
142	    ui: {
143	      ...currentUi,
144	      editSettings: toJson(settings),

146	      editMode: settings.editMode,

148	  };
149	
150	  const { error: updateError } = await supabase().from('generations')
151	    .update({ params: updatedParams })
152	    .eq('id', generationId);
153	
154	  if (updateError) {
155	    throw new Error(`Failed to save settings: ${updateError.message}`);
156	  }
```

```
11	  entityId: string | null;
12	  enabled: boolean;

30	  defaults: T;

34	  loadedSettingsRef: MutableRefObject<T | null>;
35	  transitionReadyWithPendingSave: () => void;

37	  setStatus: (s: AutoSaveStatus) => void;

39	}

41	export function useCustomModeLoad<T extends object>(ctx: CustomModeLoadContext<T>) {
42	  const {
43	    isCustomMode,
44	    entityId,
45	    enabled,
46	    statusRef,
47	    defaults,
48	    debouncedSave,
49	    customLoadRef,
50	    currentEntityIdRef,
51	    isLoadingRef,
52	    transitionReadyWithPendingSave,
53	    applyLoadedData,
54	    setStatus,
55	    setError,
56	  } = ctx;
57	
58	  useEffect(() => {
59	    if (!isCustomMode || !entityId || !enabled) {
60	      return;
61	    }
62	    if (statusRef.current !== 'idle' && statusRef.current !== 'loading') {
63	      return;
64	    }
65	
66	    if (debouncedSave.hasPendingFor(entityId)) {
67	      transitionReadyWithPendingSave();
68	      return;
69	    }
70	
71	    setStatus('loading');
72	    isLoadingRef.current = true;
73	
74	    customLoadRef.current!(entityId)
75	      .then((loaded) => {
76	        if (currentEntityIdRef.current !== entityId) {
77	          return;
78	        }
79	
80	        if (debouncedSave.hasPendingFor(entityId)) {
81	          isLoadingRef.current = false;
82	          transitionReadyWithPendingSave();
83	          return;
84	        }
85	
86	        isLoadingRef.current = false;
87	        applyLoadedData(loaded ? { ...defaults, ...loaded } : defaults, !!loaded);
88	      })
89	      .catch((err) => {
90	        normalizeAndPresentError(err, { context: 'useAutoSaveSettings.load', showToast: false });
91	        setStatus('error');
92	        isLoadingRef.current = false;
93	        setError(err as Error);
94	      });
95	  }, [isCustomMode, entityId, enabled, defaults, debouncedSave]);
96	}
97	
98	export function useReactQueryModeLoad<T extends object>(ctx: ReactQueryModeLoadContext<T>) {
99	  const {
100	    isCustomMode,
101	    entityId,
102	    enabled,
103	    statusRef,
104	    defaults,
105	    dbSettings,
106	    rqIsLoading,
107	    debouncedSave,
108	    loadedSettingsRef,
109	    transitionReadyWithPendingSave,
110	    setSettings,
111	    setStatus,
112	    setError,
113	  } = ctx;
114	
115	  useEffect(() => {
116	    if (isCustomMode || !entityId || !enabled) {
117	      return;
118	    }
119	
120	    const currentStatus = statusRef.current;
121	    if (rqIsLoading) {
122	      if (currentStatus === 'idle') {
123	        setStatus('loading');
124	      }
125	      return;
126	    }
127	
128	    if (currentStatus === 'saving') {
129	      return;
130	    }
131	
132	    if (debouncedSave.hasPendingFor(entityId)) {
133	      if (currentStatus !== 'ready') {
134	        transitionReadyWithPendingSave();
135	      }
136	      return;
137	    }
138	
139	    const loadedSettings: T = { ...defaults, ...(dbSettings || {}) };
140	    const clonedSettings = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(loadedSettings));
141	
142	    if (loadedSettingsRef.current && deepEqual(clonedSettings, loadedSettingsRef.current)) {
143	      if (currentStatus !== 'ready') {
144	        setStatus('ready');
145	      }
146	      return;
147	    }
148	
149	    setSettings(clonedSettings);
150	    loadedSettingsRef.current = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(clonedSettings));
151	    setStatus('ready');
152	    setError(null);
153	  }, [isCustomMode, entityId, rqIsLoading, dbSettings, defaults, enabled, debouncedSave]);
154	}
```

```
4	type AutoSaveStatus = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'saving' | 'error';
5	
6	function cloneSettings<T>(data: T): T {
7	  return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(data));
8	}
9	
10	interface TransitionReadyWithPendingSaveInput<T extends object> {
11	  setStatus: (status: AutoSaveStatus) => void;
12	  debouncedSave: ReturnType<typeof useDebouncedSettingsSave<T>>;
13	  saveImmediateRef: MutableRefObject<(settingsToSave?: T) => Promise<void>>;
14	  debounceMs: number;
15	}
16	
17	export function transitionReadyWithPendingSave<T extends object>({
18	  setStatus,
19	  debouncedSave,
20	  saveImmediateRef,
21	  debounceMs,
22	}: TransitionReadyWithPendingSaveInput<T>): void {
23	  setStatus('ready');
24	  debouncedSave.cancelPendingSave();
25	  const toSave = debouncedSave.pendingSettingsRef.current!;
26	  debouncedSave.saveTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(async () => {
27	    try {
28	      await saveImmediateRef.current(toSave);
29	    } catch {
30	      // surface handled at save layer; keep transition helper side-effect only
31	    }
32	  }, debounceMs);
33	}
34	
35	interface ApplyLoadedDataInput<T extends object> {
36	  data: T;
37	  hadPersistedData: boolean;
38	  isCustomMode: boolean;
39	  setSettings: Dispatch<SetStateAction<T>>;
40	  loadedSettingsRef: MutableRefObject<T | null>;
41	  setHasPersistedData: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
42	  setStatus: (status: AutoSaveStatus) => void;
43	  setError: (error: Error | null) => void;
44	}

46	export function applyLoadedDataState<T extends object>({
47	  data,
48	  hadPersistedData,
49	  isCustomMode,
50	  setSettings,
51	  loadedSettingsRef,
52	  setHasPersistedData,
53	  setStatus,

66	interface ApplyEntityChangeStateInput<T extends object> {
67	  entityId: string | null;
68	  previousEntityId: string | null;
69	  currentEntityIdRef: MutableRefObject<string | null>;
70	  defaults: T;
71	  isCustomMode: boolean;
72	  rqIsLoading: boolean;
73	  dbSettings: T | undefined;
74	  setSettings: Dispatch<SetStateAction<T>>;
75	  setStatus: (status: AutoSaveStatus) => void;
76	  setHasPersistedData: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
77	  loadedSettingsRef: MutableRefObject<T | null>;
78	  setError: (error: Error | null) => void;
79	}
80	
81	export function applyEntityChangeState<T extends object>({
82	  entityId,
83	  previousEntityId,
84	  currentEntityIdRef,
85	  defaults,
86	  isCustomMode,
87	  rqIsLoading,
88	  dbSettings,
89	  setSettings,
90	  setStatus,
91	  setHasPersistedData,
92	  loadedSettingsRef,
93	  setError,
94	}: ApplyEntityChangeStateInput<T>): void {
95	  if (entityId === previousEntityId) {
96	    return;
97	  }
98	
99	  currentEntityIdRef.current = entityId;
100	  if (!entityId) {
101	    setSettings(defaults);
102	    setStatus('idle');
103	    setHasPersistedData(false);
104	    loadedSettingsRef.current = null;
105	    return;
106	  }
107	
108	  if (previousEntityId) {
109	    setHasPersistedData(false);
110	    if (!isCustomMode && !rqIsLoading && dbSettings) {
111	      const loaded = { ...defaults, ...(dbSettings as Record<string, unknown>) } as T;
112	      const cloned = cloneSettings(loaded);
113	      setSettings(cloned);
114	      loadedSettingsRef.current = cloneSettings(cloned);
115	      setStatus('ready');
116	      setError(null);
117	      return;
118	    }
119	
120	    setSettings(defaults);
121	    setStatus('loading');
122	    loadedSettingsRef.current = null;
123	  }
124	}
```

> AGENT

Short answer: I don't see a clean single cause, but I have a strong suspect.

**Likely cause**: entity-change races in the auto-save persistence. The prompt lives in `useAutoSaveSettings` state, keyed on `generationId` (via `useEditSettingsPersistence` → `useGenerationEditSettings`). When the `entityId`/`generationId` underneath the panel flips momentarily, `applyEntityChangeState` (autoSaveSettingsHelpers.ts:108-122) resets `settings` back to defaults and flips status to `'loading'`. Typing still *works* during loading (updateField writes optimistically), but if the load resolves with persisted data and pending-tracking misses (because status went `ready→saving→ready` while you were typing, clearing the pending flag), `applyLoadedData` at autoSaveSettingsLoaders.ts:87 wipes the textarea.

Specific triggers that flip `actualGenerationId` / `generationId` mid-edit:
- Creating/accepting a variant (`setActiveVariantId` side effects → env.actualGenerationId recompute).
- The `onSaveSuccess` invalidation in useGenerationEditSettings.ts:200 refetching generation detail right after you type, then a parent prop shifts.
- Navigation between images without closing the lightbox.

One secondary smell: `EMPTY_FORM` in ImageEditFormContext.tsx:53 has no-op setters. If EditModePanel ever renders outside `ImageEditFormProvider` (e.g. in `InlineEditView` without proper wiring), typing is silently dropped.

Want me to add `console.log('[EditPrompt]', {status, entityId, value})` instrumentation in `updateField` + `applyEntityChangeState` so you can catch it next time it happens? That'll be faster than guessing further.

> DEVELOPER

Is there some kind of poor structure here that could be problematic

> AGENT

Yes — a few real structural smells here:

**1. Four layers of indirection for one string.**
Textarea → `EditModePanel` → `useEditModePanelState` → `ImageEditFormContext` → `useImageEditOrchestrator` → `useInpainting` (wraps the setter again with fallback) → `useEditSettingsPersistence` → `useGenerationEditSettings` → `useAutoSaveSettings` → `useDebouncedSettingsSave` → Supabase.

Every layer re-wraps setters, adds a fallback, or renames fields (`prompt` ↔ `inpaintPrompt`). Each re-wrap is a place a stale closure, no-op setter, or identity change can silently break typing. You can't reason about "what happens when I press a key" without reading 10 files.

**2. Defaults-as-noops (EMPTY_FORM) is a footgun.**
`useImageEditFormSafe` returns a context with `setInpaintPrompt: () => {}` when no provider is present. That's a silent failure mode — typing appears to work (cursor moves) but nothing happens. Safer: throw, or make the hook unsafe-by-default and force consumers to opt into the fallback.

**3. Render-time entity reset + effect-time init, split across files.**
`useEditSettingsPersistence.ts:110-114` mutates refs during render, `applyEntityChangeState` calls `setSettings(defaults)` also during render, and `useCustomModeLoad` does async loading in an effect. Three separate places decide what the current state should be, coordinated by refs. The comments acknowledge it's fragile ("must NOT be an effect", "sanctioned React pattern"). Pending-tracking is the only thing keeping user input safe, and it's easy to miss edge cases.

**4. Dual source of truth: generation DB + local optimistic state.**
Every keystroke → debounced DB write → `invalidateQueries` → refetch → potential state overwrite. You've papered over the race with pendingSettingsRef + edit-version checks, but the underlying shape (auto-save a free-text field on every keystroke to a remote DB) is the root cause. A prompt doesn't need to be persisted until *submit* or blur — the persistence is what creates all the race conditions.

**5. Prop/context hybrid.**
`EditModePanel` accepts both `stateOverrides` props AND reads context. `useEditModePanelState` does `imageEditState ?? contextCanvas` per-slice. Means the same component behaves differently depending on whether it's mounted inside `ImageLightbox` or `InlineEditView`, and you can mix the two (some state from props, some from context) without realizing.

**Biggest win for the user-visible bug**: stop persisting the prompt to the DB on every keystroke. Persist on submit/blur. That single change would delete most of `useDebouncedSettingsSave`, the pending-ref dance, and the entity-change race — and almost certainly fix the "can't type" symptom.

> AGENT

That's a much more diagnostic clue — not a state bug, a **focus/overlay bug**.

"Select instantly closes on open" + "can't type in textarea" = something else on the page has a focus trap or an invisible overlay eating pointer events. The prompt state is fine; the DOM is hostile.

Top suspects in this repo:

**1. A Radix modal stuck open/mid-close.** `LoraSelectorModal` is rendered at EditModePanel.tsx:476 inside `<Suspense>`, controlled by `editLoraManager.isLoraModalOpen`. Radix Dialog uses `FocusScope trapped` + sets `pointer-events: none` on `document.body` while open. If the flag gets stuck true, or if the modal unmounts mid-close (Suspense boundary flipping back while it's animating), the body style never gets cleaned up. Classic symptom: Select opens, immediately loses focus to the trap, closes.

**2. Known Radix bug: `pointer-events: none` leaks onto `<body>`.** When any Radix Dialog/Popover/Select closes during a rerender that unmounts it, the cleanup `useLayoutEffect` sometimes doesn't run. Body stays non-interactive. You can verify next time it happens: open devtools → inspect `<body>` → look for inline `pointer-events: none` or `aria-hidden="true"`. If present, that's the whole bug.

**3. Tooltip/Popover with `modal` prop.** Less likely but worth a look — any `<Popover modal>` or `<Dialog>` higher up (task details panel, variant popover) could trap focus.

**4. Voice input.** `onVoiceActiveStateChange={fieldActions.setIsAIInputActive}` — if voice activation gets stuck "active", it may be rendering an overlay that captures focus. But this wouldn't affect the Select, so probably not it.

**Fast diagnosis next time it happens**: in devtools console, run
```js
document.body.style.pointerEvents
document.querySelectorAll('[data-state="open"]')
document.querySelectorAll('[aria-hidden="true"]')
```
If body has `pointer-events: none`, or there's an `[data-state="open"]` element you didn't open, that's your culprit. `document.body.style.pointerEvents = ''` will unstick it immediately as a sanity check.

Want me to look at how `LoraSelectorModal` handles its open/close and whether the Suspense boundary could be the unmount-mid-close trigger?

> AGENT

Found it. Look at LoraSelectorModal.tsx:67-72:

```jsx
if (!isOpen) {
  return null;  // ← early return
}

return (
  <Dialog open={isOpen} onOpenChange={onClose}>
```

**This is the bug.** Base UI's `Dialog` (like Radix) cleans up its focus scope and body `pointer-events: none` lock in the `open: true → false` transition. But here, when `isOpen` flips to false, the component returns `null` on the *same render*, so `<Dialog>` unmounts while still in `open={true}` state — the cleanup never runs. Result: body stays pointer-events-none, focus scope stays trapped on a DOM node that no longer exists.

Symptoms that now make sense:
- Textarea won't take keystrokes → focus scope is trapping focus to a dead node.
- Select opens then instantly closes → the same focus trap pulls focus back on the next tick, closing the Select's popup.
- "Sometimes" → only after you've opened and closed the LoRA modal.
- Anywhere else on the page is also probably subtly broken (hover states, pointer events).

Additional triggers in EditModePanel.tsx:474-487:
```jsx
{editLoraManager && (
  <Suspense fallback={null}>
    <LoraSelectorModal ... />
```
If `editLoraManager` becomes falsy while `isOpen` is true (swapping images, mode change), the whole modal unmounts without ever rendering `open={false}` first. Same bug, different trigger.

**Fix**: remove the early return. Let Dialog render with `open={false}` so it can clean up:

```jsx
// Delete lines 67-69 (the if (!isOpen) return null)

return (
  <Dialog open={isOpen} onOpenChange={onClose}>
    ...
  </Dialog>
);
```

If you want to keep the heavy children unmounted for perf, gate the *content*, not the Dialog:

```jsx
<Dialog open={isOpen} onOpenChange={onClose}>
  {isOpen && (
    <DialogContent>...</DialogContent>
  )}
</Dialog>
```

**Verify next time it happens**: in devtools console check `document.body.style.pointerEvents` — if it's `'none'`, this is 100% confirmed. Clearing it (`document.body.style.pointerEvents = ''`) will instantly unblock typing and the Select.

Also worth grepping the rest of the codebase for the same pattern — it's likely repeated in other modals:

> DEVELOPER

Are there structural smells we should clean up in any case?

> AGENT

Yes — beyond the modal bug, a few structural smells worth cleaning up regardless:

**1. Defensive early-return-before-Dialog pattern.**
Both `LoraSelectorModal` and `PhaseConfigSelectorModal` do `if (!isOpen) return null` above a `<Dialog open={isOpen}>`. It's a footgun that bypasses the library's close lifecycle. Rule of thumb for Base UI/Radix modals: **never conditionally unmount the `<Dialog>` itself based on `open` — always let it render both states, or only gate heavy children**. Worth a lint rule or code comment in `ui/dialog.tsx`.

**2. No-op default context (`EMPTY_FORM`).**
`useImageEditFormSafe` returning silent no-op setters is the exact pattern that makes "can't type" bugs invisible. If a consumer forgets the provider, nothing breaks visibly — typing just drops on the floor. Either throw when context is missing, or rename to `useImageEditFormOrNoop` so the risk is at the call site.

**3. Per-keystroke DB persistence of a free-text field.**
The whole pending-ref / edit-version / race-protection machinery in `useDebouncedSettingsSave` exists to work around the fact that every keystroke writes to Supabase. Persist on blur/submit and most of that complexity disappears along with its race conditions.

**4. Hybrid props-or-context in `EditModePanel`.**
`stateOverrides` let you pass some slices as props while others come from context. Two rendering paths, one component — easy to get a half-wired mount. Pick one: pure props, or a separate `<StandaloneEditModePanel>` wrapper that supplies a real provider.

**5. Setter re-wrapping through many layers.**
`setInpaintPrompt` exists in FormContext, orchestrator, `useInpainting` (with fallback-to-local-state via `incomingSet ?? fallbackSet`), and persistence. Each layer adds a `useCallback` with subtle identity semantics. Consolidate: the prompt has one owner (persistence), everyone else reads/writes it directly.

**6. Render-time state mutation + ref-coordinated load effects.**
`useEditSettingsPersistence.ts:110-114` mutates refs during render; `applyEntityChangeState` calls `setSettings` during render; `useCustomModeLoad` does async loading in an effect. Three places decide "what should state be for this entity," coordinated by refs with comments that say "must NOT be an effect." That's a rewrite candidate — likely a single `useSyncExternalStore`-style or `useReducer` owner would be clearer and safer.

**7. `EditModePanel.tsx` is ~490 lines doing layout + six modes + two LoRA UIs + advanced settings.**
The IIFE-in-JSX blocks (lines 185, 253, 319) are a tell. Each `editMode` branch wants to be its own small component receiving only what it needs. Would also make the focus-trap class of bug easier to spot, because the mode panels wouldn't share a mount.

**8. Duplicate file-cleanup pattern worth linting.**
The `if (!open) return null; return <Dialog open={open}>` pattern in two modals suggests a copy-paste template. Grep for it periodically or add an ESLint rule against the combo.

Of these, **#1 and #2 are cheap wins that prevent whole bug classes**. #3 is the biggest architectural debt. #5 and #7 are the daily-friction ones that make bugs like "can't type" take an afternoon to track down instead of ten minutes.

10. **Grep audit once a quarter** for new no-op default contexts (pattern: `setX: () => {}` in a fallback const).

# Megaplan
Route every step through the `megaplan` CLI. Never call agents directly.
Before the first CLI call, resolve a working launcher and reuse it for the whole run. Do not assume `megaplan` itself is on `PATH`; command presence alone is not enough. Prove the launcher works by successfully running a harmless CLI call with it first. In the instructions below, treat `<launcher>` as that verified command.
Launcher resolution order:
1. Try `python -m megaplan config show`.
2. If that fails, try `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan config show`.
3. If that fails, try `uv run python -m megaplan config show`.
4. If that fails, try a version-selected shim such as `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 megaplan config show`.
5. Only use bare `megaplan ...` if that exact form already succeeded during this check.
## Triage
Pick the right level based on the task:
- **Skip megaplan**: single-file fixes, bug fixes with clear cause, simple refactors, config changes, adding tests for existing code. Just do it.
- **Light**: multi-file changes with clear scope, well-understood features, straightforward additions. One critique pass, no gate, no review.
- **Standard** (default for megaplan): cross-cutting changes touching many subsystems, unfamiliar codebase areas, ambiguous requirements, changes with high breakage risk, or anything where the plan itself needs debate.
- **Heavy**: high-stakes changes where getting it wrong is expensive — security-critical code, data migrations, public API changes. Uses the same visible `prep` phase but with 8 critique checks instead of 4.

Default to standard unless the task is clearly simple enough for light. Do not ask the user to choose robustness — pick it yourself based on the above. Only ask execution mode (auto-approve or review) when using megaplan.
## Start
Run `<launcher> config show` before `init`. If `raw_config.execution.auto_approve` is explicitly present, do not ask the execution-mode question and honor that configured override, including configured `false`. If that raw key is absent, ask execution mode (auto-approve or review) before `init`. In the same config check, respect `execution.robustness` as a settable override when it is configured; otherwise pick robustness yourself per the triage guidance above.
```bash
<launcher> init --project-dir "$PROJECT_DIR" [--auto-approve] [--robustness light|standard|heavy] "$IDEA"
```
Report the plan name, execution mode, robustness, current state, and next step.
## Workflow
Run the loop in this order:
1. `prep`
2. `plan`
3. `critique`
4. `gate`
5. `revise` when gate recommends iteration
6. `finalize`
7. `execute`
8. `review`
Use `next_step` and `valid_next` for CLI routing. After `gate`, follow `orchestrator_guidance` instead of manually interpreting gate signals.
At `--robustness light`, the loop is: `plan` → `critique` → `revise` → `finalize` → `execute`. There is no prep, no gate, and no review.
At `--robustness standard`, the loop is: `prep` → `plan` → `critique` → `gate` → ...
At `--robustness heavy`, the loop is also `prep` → `plan` → `critique` → `gate` → ... but uses 8 critique checks instead of 4.
## Step Rules
- `plan`: inspect the repository first; produce the plan plus `questions`, `assumptions`, and `success_criteria`. Each criterion is `{"criterion": "...", "priority": "must|should|info"}`. `must` = hard gate (reviewer blocks), `should` = quality target (reviewer flags but doesn't block), `info` = human reference (reviewer skips).
- `prep`: make repository investigation explicit before planning. Respect `skip: true` when the task is already concrete enough.
- `critique`: surface concrete flags with concern, evidence, category, and severity; reuse open flag IDs; call out scope creep. Also validate that success criteria priorities are well-calibrated — `must` criteria should be verifiable yes/no, subjective goals should be `should`.
- `gate`: read the response, warnings, and `orchestrator_guidance`. (Skipped at light robustness.)
- `revise`: show the delta, flags addressed, and flags remaining. At light robustness, routes to `finalize`; otherwise loops back through `critique` and `gate`.
- `review`: judge success against the success criteria and the user's intent, not plan elegance. Only block on `must` criteria failures. `should` failures are flagged but don't require rework. `info` criteria are waived.
## Gate Principle
The gate response tells the orchestrator what to do next. Follow `orchestrator_guidance` unless you have a concrete reason to disagree after investigating the repository or plan artifacts yourself.
Investigate before disagreeing: read the current plan and critique artifacts, check the project code to verify whether a flagged issue is real, or use `megaplan status --plan <name>` / `megaplan audit --plan <name>`.
If you disagree with the guidance, explain why briefly and use an override. Do not manually reinterpret score trajectory, flag quality, or loop state when the gate already did that work for you.
## Execute
- After a successful gate, run `megaplan finalize` to produce the execution-ready briefing document.
- In auto-approve mode, run `megaplan execute --confirm-destructive` after finalize.
- In review mode, pause at the finalize-to-execute checkpoint and wait for explicit approval before running:
```bash
megaplan execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved
```
## Long-Running Execution
For plans with multiple batches, use per-batch mode to drive execution incrementally:
```bash
megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 1
megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 2
# ... continue until all batches complete
```
Between batches, poll progress:
```bash
megaplan progress --plan <name>
```
Per-batch mode uses global batch numbering (1-indexed, computed from ALL tasks). Each `--batch N` call:
- Validates that batches 1..N-1 are complete
- Executes only batch N's tasks
- Writes `execution_batch_N.json` as evidence
- On the final batch, produces aggregate `execution.json` and transitions to `executed`
Timeout recovery: re-run the same `--batch N`. The harness checks prerequisite completion and merges only untracked tasks.
Note: `progress` shows completed state only (between-batch granularity). With per-batch mode, each batch is a separate CLI call, so the orchestrator has full visibility.
## Overrides
- `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."`
- `megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."`
- `megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]`
- `megaplan override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."`
`force-proceed` is available from `critiqued` (routes to finalize, not execute). `replan` is available from `gated`, `finalized`, or `critiqued`. `add-note` is safe from any active state.
## Replan
Use `replan` when the orchestrator itself needs to edit the plan directly instead of asking the revise worker to do it.
```bash
megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "expanding scope" --note "Also clean up the display layer"
```
After `replan`, read the returned plan file, edit it directly, then run `megaplan critique`.
## Step Editing
Use `step` when you need to insert, remove, or reorder step sections (`## Step N:` or `### Step N:`) without hand-editing the markdown.
```bash
megaplan step add --plan <name> --after S3 "Add regression coverage for the parser"
megaplan step remove --plan <name> S4
megaplan step move --plan <name> S4 --after S2
```
Each edit writes a new same-iteration plan artifact, preserves the latest plan meta questions/success criteria/assumptions, and resets the plan to `planned` so it re-enters critique.
## Sessions And Autonomy
- Agents default to persistent sessions.
- `--fresh`: start a new persistent session.
- `--ephemeral`: one-off call with no saved session.
- `--persist`: explicit persistent mode.
- Keep moving and show results at each step.
- Only pause at finalize to execute in review mode.
## Configuration
View current defaults with `megaplan config show`. Override with `megaplan config set <key> <value>`. Reset with `megaplan config reset`.
When routing or behavior depends on config, check `megaplan config show` and respect user overrides instead of assuming defaults.
Settable execution keys: `execution.auto_approve`, `execution.robustness`.
## Commands
```bash
megaplan status --plan <name>
megaplan progress --plan <name>
megaplan watch --plan <name>
megaplan audit --plan <name>
megaplan list
megaplan prep --plan <name>
megaplan plan --plan <name>
megaplan critique --plan <name>
megaplan revise --plan <name>
megaplan gate --plan <name>
megaplan finalize --plan <name>
megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive [--batch N]
megaplan review --plan <name>
megaplan step add --plan <name> [--after S<N>] "description"
megaplan step remove --plan <name> S<N>
megaplan step move --plan <name> S<N> --after S<M>
megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."
megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]
megaplan override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."
megaplan config show
megaplan config set <key> <value>
megaplan config reset
```

## Subagent Mode
This appendix is Claude-specific. It adds a subagent path; subagent mode is the default for Claude.

### Activation
- Default to subagent unless an inline override is explicitly set for this run or `megaplan config show` reports `"orchestration": {"mode": "inline"}`.
- Per-run override wins over config. If the run explicitly says `inline`, stay inline even when config prefers `subagent`.
- Use subagent mode for long multi-phase runs where keeping the outer conversation clean matters, especially auto-approve runs.
- Prefer inline mode for small edits, quick clarifications, or any run where the user wants to watch each phase in the main thread.

### Launch
When subagent mode is active, the outer skill becomes a launcher plus breakpoint relay. Start a Claude Code Agent with:
- `description`: `Run megaplan autonomously for {PROJECT_DIR}`
- `prompt`: fill the template below with `{IDEA}`, `{PROJECT_DIR}`, `{AUTO_APPROVE}`, `{AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG}`, `{ROBUSTNESS}`, and `{ROBUSTNESS_FLAG}`
- `run_in_background: true` when `{AUTO_APPROVE}` is true; otherwise foreground is fine
- Expand `{AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG}` to an empty string when `raw_config.execution.auto_approve` is explicitly set; otherwise expand it to `--auto-approve` for auto-approve runs and an empty string for review runs.
- Expand `{ROBUSTNESS_FLAG}` to an empty string when `raw_config.execution.robustness` is explicitly set; otherwise expand it to `--robustness {ROBUSTNESS}`.
- After editing this source file, rerun `megaplan setup --force` so installed `SKILL.md` files pick up the refreshed appendix.

### Outer Skill Handling
- Decide inline vs subagent before starting the workflow.
- In subagent mode, launch the agent, wait for either `BREAKPOINT:` or `COMPLETE:`, and keep the main thread thin.
- Support inject-after by letting the background subagent continue while the user runs `megaplan override add-note`; the next phase boundary picks it up from `megaplan status`.
- Support kill-and-inject by stopping the running subagent, appending a note with `megaplan override add-note`, and relaunching a new subagent on the same plan.
- When a breakpoint arrives, relay the summary to the user, collect the answer, and resume the same agent with `SendMessage` when possible.
- Parse only the explicit breakpoint header, not incidental text, when deciding whether the agent stopped intentionally.
- When completion arrives, report the final result back to the user without replaying every internal phase.

### Agent Prompt Template
```text
You are the autonomous megaplan runner for this single run.

Project: {PROJECT_DIR}
Idea: {IDEA}
Execution mode: {AUTO_APPROVE}
Robustness: {ROBUSTNESS}

## 1. Role & Mission
Your job is to drive the megaplan workflow through the CLI until the run finishes or a defined breakpoint requires the outer conversation.

Always follow these priorities, in order:
1. The latest user direction relayed through notes or resume messages.
2. The live CLI state from `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
3. The workflow and breakpoint rules in this template.
4. Your own memory of earlier turns.

Always do these things:
- Operate through the `megaplan` CLI only. Do not call workers or agents directly.
- Keep the outer conversation clean. Do not ask for routine confirmation.
- Use `next_step` and `valid_next` for routing. If memory and CLI state disagree, trust CLI state.
- Follow `orchestrator_guidance` after `gate` unless you have a concrete reason to disagree after checking plan artifacts or repository evidence yourself.
- Treat user notes as authoritative.

Never do these things:
- Do not run the workflow manually outside the CLI.
- Do not skip required phases for the selected robustness level.
- Do not emit a breakpoint unless one of the breakpoint rules below says to.

## 2. Startup
Start the run like this:
1. Use empty-string expansion for `{AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG}` and `{ROBUSTNESS_FLAG}` whenever the corresponding `raw_config.execution` key is explicitly set.
2. Run `megaplan init --project-dir "{PROJECT_DIR}" {AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG} {ROBUSTNESS_FLAG} "{IDEA}"`.
3. Capture the returned plan name.
4. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line immediately after init and before any `BREAKPOINT:` or `COMPLETE:`.
5. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
6. From then on, use that plan name for every command.

At startup and after every later resume:
- Read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array before acting. Do not track note cursors or indexes; always read the full array.
- Treat all notes as context. If the newest note changes direction, treat that note as the new intent and decide whether to continue, revise, replan, or break out.
- If `active_step` is present, treat it as an in-flight phase marker rather than a completed step. Use `last_step` for the most recent completed phase.

## 3. Phase Routing by Robustness
Use the workflow below exactly.

Light robustness:
- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> revise -> finalize -> execute -> done`
- There is no `gate`.
- There is no `review`.
- `prep` may return `skip: true`; that still counts as the visible prep phase.
- After the light `revise`, the CLI moves to `gated`, so the next command is `finalize`.
- After `execute`, the CLI will end the run.

Standard robustness:
- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> gate`
- Then follow the gate decision tree below.
- `prep` may return `skip: true`; do not skip the command yourself.
- When you reach `gated`, run `finalize`.
- Then run `execute`.
- Then run `review`.
- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, the workflow becomes `finalized -> execute -> review` again until review passes or the CLI reaches its cap.

Heavy robustness:
- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> gate`
- `prep` may still return `skip: true`, but the phase remains visible in the CLI state/history.
- After that, heavy follows the same gate, finalize, execute, and review behavior as standard.

Gate decision tree for standard and heavy:
- Condition 1: `gate_unset`
  Trigger: state is `critiqued` and `valid_next` includes `gate`.
  Action: run `megaplan gate --plan <name>`.
- Condition 2: `gate_iterate`
  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `ITERATE`, so `valid_next` includes `revise` but not `override force-proceed`.
  Action: run `megaplan revise --plan <name>`, then continue back through `critique` and `gate`.
- Condition 3: `gate_escalate`
  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `ESCALATE`, so `valid_next` offers `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
  Action: stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE`.
- Condition 4: `gate_proceed_blocked`
  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `PROCEED`, but preflight still blocked execution, so state stays `critiqued` and `valid_next` offers `revise` plus `override force-proceed`.
  Action: do not finalize yet. Use `orchestrator_guidance` plus `preflight_results` to fix the blocking checks through `revise`. On iteration 1, the guidance text may stay generic, so inspect `preflight_results` yourself before revising. If the blocker cannot be resolved safely without a user decision, stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_BLOCKED`.
- Condition 5: `gate_proceed`
  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `PROCEED` and preflight passed, so state becomes `gated`.
  Action: run `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`.

Review routing for standard and heavy:
- If `review` succeeds, the run is done.
- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, the CLI moves back to `finalized` with `next_step` set to `execute`.
- When that happens, run `execute` again, then `review` again.
- This rework loop is capped by the CLI at 3 `needs_rework` cycles. If the cap is hit, the CLI force-proceeds to done and records the issue.

## 4. After Every Phase
After every phase command, immediately run:
`megaplan status --plan <name>`

Then do all of the following before choosing the next command:
- Re-read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array; worker agents already receive all notes automatically.
- Check whether the newest note changes direction before the next CLI call.
- If the last phase was `gate`, treat `orchestrator_guidance` as a literal routing hint. Its lead text will be one of these exact forms:
  `First iteration; follow gate recommendation: <recommendation>.`
  `Plan passed gate and preflight. Proceed to finalize.`
  `Gate says PROCEED but preflight blocked. Fix: <checks>.`
  `Gate escalated. Ask the user: force-proceed, add-note, or abort.`
  `Score plateaued with recurring critiques the loop can't fix. Consider force-proceeding: \`megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name>\``
  `Score improving (<previous> -> <current>). Continue to revise.`
  `Score worsening (<previous> -> <current>). Investigate; the loop may be diverging.`
  `Gate recommends another iteration. Revise the plan.`
- On iteration 1, the first form takes precedence over the more specific `PROCEED` or `ESCALATE` strings, so use `recommendation`, `valid_next`, and `preflight_results` together.
- If `orchestrator_guidance` includes extra text after that lead string, treat it as appended hints about unresolved flags, recurring critiques, or scope creep.
- If the phase response and `status` disagree, trust `status`.
- If the next move is unclear, prefer the explicit `valid_next` list over your own reconstruction of the state machine.

## 5. Breakpoints
Use a breakpoint only for the cases in this section. Format every breakpoint exactly like this:

`BREAKPOINT: <type>`
`Plan: <name>`
`State: <state>`
`Summary: <short reason>`
`Context: <artifacts, warnings, or the exact user decision needed>`

Breakpoint types and triggers:
- `GATE_ESCALATE`
  Trigger: gate recommends `ESCALATE`, or `valid_next` offers `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
- `GATE_BLOCKED`
  Trigger: you are in the `gate_proceed_blocked` branch and need the outer user to decide between more revision and `override force-proceed`.
- `EXECUTE_APPROVAL`
  Trigger: `finalize` succeeded in review mode and `execute` now requires explicit approval.
- `PHASE_ESCALATE`
  Trigger: a non-execute phase still fails after the required retry, or it returns unusable output twice.
- `EXECUTE_ESCALATE`
  Trigger: `execute` reaches the no-progress cap, or repeated blocking/timeouts prevent forward progress.

## 6. Safeguards
Non-execute safeguards:
- If any non-execute phase fails, returns unusable output, or clearly lands in a bad session state, retry that same phase once with `--fresh`.
- If the exact same error appears twice in a row for the same phase, the next retry must use `--fresh`.
- If the phase still fails after the required fresh retry, stop with `BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE`.

Execute safeguards:
- Count whether each `execute` call creates forward progress.
- Forward progress means new completed tasks, a completed batch, or a state advance that clearly moves the run closer to done.
- If you hit 3 consecutive `execute` attempts without forward progress, stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE`.
- If `execute` times out or is blocked, retry up to that same 3-attempt cap.

Review safeguards:
- `needs_rework` is a normal workflow branch, not a phase failure.
- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, do not break out. Follow the rework loop and run `execute` again from `finalized`.
- If `review` returns blocked instead of a real verdict, the CLI keeps the run in `executed` with `next_step` set to `review`.
- If `review` returns blocked or otherwise unusable output, treat that as a review-phase problem and apply the non-execute retry rule.

Notes and interruption safeguards:
- If the outer skill kills and relaunches you, start fresh with no reliable memory from the prior run.
- After any note injection or relaunch, run `megaplan status --plan <name>` immediately, read the full `notes` array, and treat all notes as context.
- Treat the most recent note as the relaunch explanation, then resume from `next_step`; the CLI state machine is the source of truth.

## 7. Resume Protocol
When the outer conversation resumes you with `SendMessage`, or when a new subagent is launched on an existing plan:
1. Re-read the message carefully.
2. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
3. Read the full `notes` array.
4. Resume from the current CLI state and `next_step`, not from memory.

Resume rules:
- If the user grants execution approval, continue directly into `execute` with the correct approval flag.
- If the user answers a gate breakpoint, translate that answer into the minimum necessary action: continue revising, `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
- If the user changes scope or intent materially, prefer `override replan`.
- After resuming, continue autonomously until the next defined breakpoint or completion.

## 7A. Note Injection from Outer Skill
- Use the stored `PLAN_NAME` for note and status calls. If it was not captured, run `megaplan list` and fall back to the most recent plan.
- Classify the user message: "add context for next phase" -> Option A, "change direction NOW" -> Option B, "just a question" -> answer without touching the run. Default to Option A unless the message clearly demands interruption.
- Option A (inject-at-boundary): run `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "<note>"`, confirm to the user, and do not `TaskStop` or `SendMessage`.
- Option B (kill+relaunch): `TaskStop` the orchestrator, run `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "<note>"`, relaunch a new orchestrator with prompt `Resume plan <name>. Run megaplan status to get current state, read all notes, and continue from where it left off.`, then confirm to the user.
- Latency: Option A can take up to one phase boundary; if that is not acceptable, the user should ask for Option B.

## 8. Execution Details
Finalize and execute:
- After `gated`, run `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`.
- In auto-approve mode, run `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`.
- In review mode, stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_APPROVAL`, then after approval run `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved`.

Per-batch execution:
- If the execution briefing or CLI response indicates per-batch execution, continue batch by batch.
- Batch numbering is global and 1-indexed.
- Use `megaplan progress --plan <name>` between batch executions.
- Re-run the same batch number after a timeout if needed; the harness will reconcile previously completed work.

Execution loop end conditions:
- Continue until all actionable tasks are complete and the workflow reaches `done`.
- Stop early only for a defined breakpoint.

## 9. Overrides & Plan Editing
Override rules:
- `megaplan override add-note` is safe from any active state when you need to record new user direction without changing state.
- `megaplan override force-proceed` from `critiqued` moves the run into `gated`. Use it only when the user clearly wants to override the gate.
- `megaplan override force-proceed` cannot bypass a missing project directory or missing success criteria.
- `megaplan override force-proceed` from `executed` moves the run to `done`. Use that only when the user explicitly accepts unresolved review issues.
- `megaplan override abort` ends the run. Use it only when the user clearly wants to stop.
- `megaplan override replan` is available from `critiqued`, `gated`, or `finalized`. Use it when the orchestrator itself needs to edit the plan directly instead of asking the revise worker to do it.

Replan behavior:
- After `override replan`, read the latest plan file, edit it directly, then continue with `critique`.

Step editing:
- `megaplan step add`, `step remove`, and `step move` are available while the run is in `planned`, `critiqued`, `gated`, or `finalized`.
- Use them when you need to insert, remove, or reorder step sections without hand-editing the markdown.
- After a step edit, re-check `status` and continue from the returned state.

## 10. Completion Format
When the workflow completes, return exactly this shape:

`COMPLETE: megaplan run finished`
`Plan: <name>`
`Final state: <state>`
`Summary: <outcome>`
`Artifacts: <key files or reports>`
`Follow-up: <only if something remains>`

## 11. Command Reference
Core commands:
- `megaplan status --plan <name>`
- `megaplan progress --plan <name>`
- `megaplan audit --plan <name>`

Workflow commands:
- `megaplan prep --plan <name>`
- `megaplan plan --plan <name>`
- `megaplan critique --plan <name>`
- `megaplan gate --plan <name>`
- `megaplan revise --plan <name>`
- `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`
- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`
- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved`
- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch N`
- `megaplan review --plan <name>`

Override and editing commands:
- `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."`
- `megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."`
- `megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]`
- `megaplan override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."`
- `megaplan step add --plan <name> --after S<N> "description"`
- `megaplan step remove --plan <name> S<N>`
- `megaplan step move --plan <name> S<N> --after S<M>`
```

Phase 1 (stop the bleeding — fixes user's "can't type in edit textbox" bug):
1. Fix `reigh-app/src/domains/lora/components/LoraSelectorModal/LoraSelectorModal.tsx:67-69` — remove `if (!isOpen) return null` early-return before `<Dialog open={isOpen}>`. Base UI Dialog cleanup doesn't run when component unmounts while open={true}, leaving body pointer-events:none and focus scope stuck — which is why the textarea can't be typed in and the model Select closes instantly when opened. If children are heavy, gate `<DialogContent>` instead of the whole Dialog.
2. Same fix in `reigh-app/src/shared/components/PhaseConfigSelectorModal/PhaseConfigSelectorModal.tsx`.
3. Add guard comment at top of `reigh-app/src/shared/components/ui/dialog.tsx` explaining the rule.
4. Make `useImageEditFormSafe` in `reigh-app/src/domains/media-lightbox/contexts/ImageEditFormContext.tsx` fail loud: rename current to `useImageEditForm` (throws when provider missing); keep a separately-named `useImageEditFormSafe` returning EMPTY_FORM for explicit opt-in callers. EMPTY_FORM's no-op setters silently drop typing if context is missing — same bug class.

Phase 2 (decouple edit panel):
5. Split `reigh-app/src/domains/media-lightbox/components/EditModePanel.tsx` (490 lines) by mode into `<TextEditPanel>`, `<InpaintPanel>`, `<AnnotatePanel>`, `<RepositionPanel>`, `<Img2ImgPanel>`, `<UpscalePanel>`. Root `EditModePanel` becomes a thin router. Eliminate the IIFE-in-JSX blocks at lines 185, 253, 319.
6. Collapse the props-vs-context hybrid: pick ONE source. Either wrap `InlineEditView` in a real `ImageEditProvider` and delete `stateOverrides`, or go pure-props and remove context reads.
7. Flatten setter re-wrapping in `reigh-app/src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/useInpainting.ts:117-123` — remove `incomingSet ?? fallbackSet` fallback. Persistence owns the prompt; everyone else reads/writes directly.

Phase 3 (architectural debt):
8. Stop persisting the prompt field to Supabase on every keystroke. Persist on blur, on generate, or on lightbox close. Other fields (sliders/toggles) stay debounced — they don't race with user typing. This lets us delete most of `reigh-app/src/shared/settings/hooks/useDebouncedSettingsSave.ts`'s pending-ref + edit-version machinery, which exists purely to work around the per-keystroke DB write race.
9. With #8 done, consolidate `useAutoSaveSettings` entity-change coordination. Right now `useEditSettingsPersistence.ts:110-114` mutates refs during render, `applyEntityChangeState` in `autoSaveSettingsHelpers.ts` calls setSettings during render, and `useCustomModeLoad` loads in an effect — three places deciding "what should state be for this entity." A `useReducer` for (entityId, status, settings) atomicizes the transition.

Phase 4 (prevent regressions):
10. Add ESLint rule (or at minimum a documented check) for the pattern `if (!open|!isOpen) return null` followed by a `<Dialog>` render.
11. Document the no-op-default-context antipattern somewhere visible (likely `reigh-app/CLAUDE.md` or a structure_detail doc).

```
 type AutoSaveStatus = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'saving' | 'error';
 
+interface AutoSaveState<T extends object> {
+  entityId: string | null;
+  settings: T;
+  status: AutoSaveStatus;
+  error: Error | null;
+  hasPersistedData: boolean;
+}
+
+type AutoSaveAction<T extends object> =
+  | {
+      type: 'ENTITY_CHANGED';
+      entityId: string | null;
+      settings: T;
+      status: AutoSaveStatus;
+      error: Error | null;
+      hasPersistedData: boolean;
+    }
+  | { type: 'LOAD_STARTED' }
+  | { type: 'LOAD_RESOLVED'; settings: T; hasPersistedData: boolean }
+  | {
+      type: 'SETTINGS_UPDATED';
+      nextSettings?: T;
+      merge?: Partial<T>;
+      status?: AutoSaveStatus;
+      error?: Error | null;
+      hasPersistedData?: boolean;
+    };
+
+function autoSaveSettingsReducer<T extends object>(
+  state: AutoSaveState<T>,
+  action: AutoSaveAction<T>
+): AutoSaveState<T> {
+  switch (action.type) {
+    case 'ENTITY_CHANGED':
+      return {
+        entityId: action.entityId,
+        settings: action.settings,
+        status: action.status,
+        error: action.error,
+        hasPersistedData: action.hasPersistedData,
+      };
+
+    case 'LOAD_STARTED':
+      return {
+        ...state,
+        status: 'loading',
+        error: null,
+      };
+
+    case 'LOAD_RESOLVED':
+      return {
+        ...state,
+        settings: action.settings,
+        status: 'ready',
+        error: null,
+        hasPersistedData: action.hasPersistedData,
+      };
+
+    case 'SETTINGS_UPDATED': {
+      const settings = action.nextSettings ?? { ...state.settings, ...action.merge };
+      return {
+        ...state,
+        settings,
+        status: action.status ?? state.status,
+        error: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(action, 'error') ? (action.error ?? null) : state.error,
+        hasPersistedData: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(action, 'hasPersistedData')
+          ? (action.hasPersistedData ?? state.hasPersistedData)
+          : state.hasPersistedData,
+      };
+    }
+
+    default:
+      return state;
+  }
+}
+
```

Quick assessment after eyeballing the diffs:

**Solid:**
- Phase 1 (LoRA modal, Phase modal, Dialog guard, `useImageEditForm` throws) — exactly as specified, small surgical diffs.
- Phase 2 split — 7 new per-mode panel files created (`TextEditPanel`, `InpaintPanel`, `AnnotatePanel`, `RepositionPanel`, `Img2ImgPanel`, `UpscalePanel`, `sharedSections`). `EditModePanel.tsx` shrank by 516 lines → thin router. Matches the brief.
- CLAUDE.md got a proper "Context hooks" section with the motivating incident documented.
- Tests were added for `useInpainting` (+41), `useImageEditOrchestrator` (+44), `InlineEditView` (+425) — not just loosened.

**Worth scrutinizing before shipping:**
1. **`useAutoSaveSettings.ts` +449 lines refactored to `useReducer`.** This is the riskiest change. It's a shared hook used by more than just media-lightbox. The diff looks clean (entity-change is atomic now, as spec'd), but it deserves a careful read and a full test run. A bug here affects every tool that persists settings.
2. **`InlineEditView.tsx` -65 lines + 425 new test lines.** The props-vs-context hybrid collapse landed, but confirm which direction was chosen (pure props vs provider-wrap) and that standalone-mode still works.
3. **`useEditSettingsPersistence.ts` +29 -18.** This was the render-time-ref-mutation smell. Make sure the reducer consolidation actually removed the fragile patterns rather than adding a layer on top.
4. **`flushTextFields` plumbing.** Phase 3's on-blur/on-close flush. Verify it's actually called on blur + lightbox close, otherwise prompts silently won't persist.

**Overall verdict**: Phase 1 is ship-ready immediately. Phases 2-3 look structurally correct but touch shared infrastructure — run the full `useAutoSaveSettings` test suite and smoke-test one or two other tools that consume it (not just media-lightbox) before merging.

> AGENT

Test results: **4508 pass / 36 fail across 19 files**. The in-scope media-lightbox + settings tests all pass. Failures are mostly in unrelated areas (TimelineEditor, TravelBetweenImages, projects, realtime) — likely pre-existing, but a few deserve a look: `useVideoLightboxRenderModel.test.tsx`, `EditImagesPage.test.tsx`, `moduleImportCoverage.test.ts`.

**Addressing your structural question:**

**Image edit / MediaLightbox edit panel** — meaningfully better now:
- `EditModePanel` went from 490-line god component to a thin router + 6 focused per-mode panels.
- Entity-change coordination in `useAutoSaveSettings` is atomic via `useReducer` — no more three-places-decide-state.
- Prompt flush is on blur/close, not per-keystroke — the race-protection machinery got to shrink.
- Dialog + context antipatterns fixed + codified in CLAUDE.md + tests.

**Video lightbox** — essentially untouched by this run. The diff shows `VideoLightbox.tsx` unchanged; only `useVideoLightboxRenderModel.tsx` got a small +2 line tweak. It inherits the benefits (Dialog rule, `useImageEditForm` pattern) but its own structure wasn't touched. Given the symptoms you reported were image-side, that's fine — but if you want the same decomposition applied to the video edit panel, that's a follow-up.

**Still-rough edges** to be aware of:
1. `useAutoSaveSettings.ts` more than doubled in size (+449 lines). It's clearer internally but still a lot of one-hook. If anything's going to need another pass later, it's this.
2. The ~20 unrelated test failures need a triage pass before merging — git-bisect them against `main` to separate regressions from pre-existing breakage.
3. `useVideoLightboxRenderModel.test.tsx` in the failure list is the one I'd check first; that one could be a real regression from the shared context changes.

Net: image-edit side is solidly restructured; video side is stable but untouched.

Editor is mounted (Timeline context available) → drop on the timeline immediately.\n * 2. Editor not mounted, first click → stage the generationId in localStorage and\n *    enter 'staged' phase (button shows a success state). No navigation.\n * 3. Editor not mounted, second click (already staged) → navigate to the editor;\n *    VideoEditorProvider drains the staged queue on mount.\n */\nexport function useAddToVideoEditor(media: GenerationRow | undefined): UseAddToVideoEditorResult {\n  const ops = useTimelineEditorOpsSafe();\n  const data = useTimelineEditorDataSafe();\n  const navigate = useNavigate();\n  const { settings: videoSettings } = useToolSettings(videoEditorSettings.id);\n\n  const generationId = media ? (getGenerationId(media) ?? media.id) : null;\n\n  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<AddToVideoEditorPhase>(() => {\n    if (!generationId) return 'idle';\n    return readPendingAdds().includes(generationId) ? 'staged' : 'idle';\n  });\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!generationId) {\n      setPhase('idle');\n      return;\n    }\n    setPhase(readPendingAdds().includes(generationId) ? 'staged' : 'idle');\n  }, [generationId]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const onStorage = (e: StorageEvent) => {\n      if (e.key !== PENDING_ADDS_STORAGE_KEY) return;\n      if (!generationId) return;\n      setPhase(readPendingAdds().includes(generationId) ? 'staged' : 'idle');\n    };\n    window.addEventListener('storage', onStorage);\n    return () => window.removeEventListener('storage', onStorage);\n  }, [generationId]);\n\n  const onClick = useCallback(() => {\n    if (!media) {\n      console.log('[AddToVideoEditor] no media — aborting');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!generationId) {\n      console.log('[AddToVideoEditor] no generationId on media', media);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (ops && data) {\n      console.log('[AddToVideoEditor] editor mounted — dropping directly', { generationId });\n      const [REDACTED]({\n        generationId,\n        variantType: media.type === 'video' ? 'video' : 'image',\n        imageUrl: media.location ?? media.imageUrl ?? '',\n        thumbUrl: media.thumbUrl ?? media.imageUrl ?? media.location ?? '',\n      });\n      if (!assetKey) {\n        console.log('[AddToVideoEditor] registerGenerationAsset returned null', { generationId });\n        toast.error('Could not register asset');\n        return;\n      }\n      const clips = data.resolvedConfig?.clips ?? [];\n      const timelineEnd = clips.reduce(\n        (max, clip) => Math.max(max, clip.at + getClipTimelineDuration(clip)),\n        0,\n      );\n      console.log('[AddToVideoEditor] dropping asset', { assetKey, timelineEnd, clipCount: clips.length });\n      ops.handleAssetDrop(assetKey, undefined, timelineEnd, true, true);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (phase === 'staged') {\n      console.log('[AddToVideoEditor] staged already — navigating to editor', { generationId });\n      const basePath = videoEditorPathWithTimeline(videoSettings?.lastTimelineId);\n      const separator = basePath.includes('?') ? '&' : '?';\n      navigate(`${basePath}${separator}${ADD_GENERATION_QUERY_PARAM}=${encodeURIComponent(generationId)}`);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const current = readPendingAdds();\n    if (!current.includes(generationId)) {\n      writePendingAdds([...current, generationId]);\n    }\n    console.log('[AddToVideoEditor] staged for next editor mount', { generationId, queueSize: current.length + 1 });\n    setPhase('staged');\n  }, [media, generationId, ops, data, navigate, videoSettings?.lastTimelineId, phase]);\n\n  return { onClick, phase };\n}\n"
```json
}
```

> AGENT

Clean. Three changes:

1. **Button now at `bottom-40` (160px up)** with `z-[70]` — well above the shot-selector popover area.

2. **Richer click log** — now includes `mediaId`, `mediaGenerationId`, `mediaType`, `hasLocation` so you can see exactly what's being passed.

3. **Variants fallback in `loadGenerationForLightbox`** — this is probably your 404 root cause. The current lookup only queries the `generations` table. If the id passed is actually a `generation_variants.id` (common when the lightbox is showing an active variant), the row won't exist in `generations` → 404 → "Could not load asset". The new fallback:
   - Uses `.maybeSingle()` instead of `.single()` (no 404 error, just null data).
   - On null, queries `generation_variants` with a join to the parent `generations`.
   - Returns the parent row with the variant's location taking precedence.

Log tags to filter next time you test: `[AddToVideoEditor]`, `[AddToVideoEditor:consume]`, `[loadGenerationForLightbox]`. You should now see which path resolves or exactly where it stops.

> AGENT

Two issues besides position:

1. **Log got cut off** — query started but you interrupted before result came back. Share the full log after my next fix and we'll see which path it hits.

2. **Real bug in the drain loop.** The effect depends on the whole `editor` object. Every clip drop mutates editor state, which recreates `editor` → effect cleanup fires → `cancelled = true` → the loop aborts after processing just the first item. The queue of 4 items partially drains, `finally` block sees cancelled, so it doesn't even clear localStorage. On next refresh, we re-stage them all again.

Switching to refs so editor stability doesn't cancel the drain:

> AGENT

Clean. Three fixes:

1. **Button at `bottom-24`** (96px) — between the too-high 40 and the too-low 16.

2. **Drain loop no longer cancels on editor re-renders.** Previously the effect depended on the whole `editor` object, so each dropped clip caused a cleanup → `cancelled = true` → loop aborted. Now:
   - Uses `editorRef.current` to always read the latest editor instance.
   - Deps narrowed to `pendingAddGenerationId` + `editor.isLoading` only.
   - `drainInFlightRef` prevents re-entry.
   - **Per-item progress tracked**: items are removed from localStorage only after each one is actually processed, not all-or-nothing.
   - 50ms breather between iterations so React commits the previous clip before the next read.

3. **New log `[AddToVideoEditor:consume] drop complete`** after each successful drop, plus `drain finished` with `{processed, remaining}` at the end.

Next test: click → navigate → share the full console. You should see:
- `draining queue` with the full list
- `loading` → `loaded` (or `null` with a specific reason from `[loadGenerationForLightbox]` log) for each item
- `dropping asset` → `drop complete` for each
- `drain finished` with processed count

If the 404 is real (row genuinely missing), the variant-fallback in `loadGenerationForLightbox` should pick it up. If THAT also fails, the log tells us exactly which lookup returned null.

Done. Each item should now go onto the same existing track (or the selected track) at the end, rather than spawning a new track per drop.

Two unrelated warnings in your log you can ignore for now:
- `<button> cannot appear as a descendant of <button>` in OverlayEditor.tsx — a separate DOM nesting issue in that file (Tooltip with `asChild` wrapping another Button probably), not from our changes.
- `TimelineSave conflict retry succeeded` — timeline persistence saw a version conflict and recovered. Expected behavior, working as designed.

> DEVELOPER

anything else concerning there?

> AGENT

Looking at the log, a few things worth mentioning — ranked by actual concern:

**Mildly concerning (ours):**

1. **All 4 drops in the first test showed `clipCount: 0, timelineEnd: 0`.** Our 50ms breather isn't long enough for `editor.resolvedConfig.clips` to reflect each prior drop. The `timelineEnd` we compute is always 0, so we're effectively ignoring our own calculation. In practice it probably still works — `handleAssetDrop` internally uses its own up-to-date `dataRef` and snaps/resolves the target, so our `time=0` argument is overridden. But the log is misleading and our calculation is cosmetic at best. If you notice clips actually stacking at time 0 instead of spreading, we'd need a different approach (e.g. drop one, `await` the state commit properly, then compute the real end). For now let's leave it unless you see stacking.

2. **`TimelineSave conflict detected` → retry succeeded.** Each drop triggers its own save, and with 4 drops back-to-back they race each other. The retry machinery handled it, but it's wasted work. A cleaner design would batch the 4 drops into a single save. Not urgent.

**Not ours — pre-existing:**

3. **`<button> cannot appear as a descendant of <button>`** in `OverlayEditor.tsx` — separate DOM nesting bug in that file, unrelated to our changes. Probably a `<Tooltip asChild>` wrapping a `<Button>` inside another `<Button>`. Worth a follow-up fix but not from this work.

4. **Three `usePersistentToolState` "no default value"** warnings for `beforeEachPromptText`, `afterEachPromptText`, `masterPrompt` — pre-existing config gap in image-generation settings.

5. **`Unknown settings [REDACTED]`** — someone's reading a settings key that isn't registered in `SETTINGS_IDS`. Pre-existing.

6. **`setTimeout handler took 85ms`** performance violation — probably one of our drops triggering downstream work. Benign.

**Summary**: nothing broken. The "timelineEnd always 0" is the only thing that might bite — test with an existing-timeline scenario (drop a clip manually, then use the film button) and confirm new ones land at the end, not stacked.

I can't pinpoint it by code search — same class of bug but different origin. Need you to run diagnostic in browser devtools next time it reproduces. **Open the lightbox, reproduce "can't type" or "Select flashes closed", then in console run:**

```js
// 1. Is body locked?
console.log('pointer-events:', document.body.style.pointerEvents);

// 2. What's claiming open state?
document.querySelectorAll('[data-state="open"]').forEach(el =>
  console.log('OPEN:', el.tagName, el.className.slice(0, 80), el));

// 3. Inert / aria-hidden regions stealing focus
console.log('inert:', document.querySelectorAll('[inert]').length);
console.log('hidden:', document.querySelectorAll('[aria-hidden="true"]').length);

// 4. Where is focus actually going
console.log('active:', document.activeElement);

// 5. Test: does unlocking body fix it?
document.body.style.pointerEvents = '';
```

Paste the output and I'll know exactly which overlay is the culprit. Specifically:
- If `pointer-events: none` → same bug class, different modal leaking. The `[data-state="open"]` list will name it.
- If no body lock but Select still won't stay open → something is stealing focus on click-away (maybe a `<Tooltip>` or `<Popover>` with `modal={true}`).
- If `document.body.style.pointerEvents = ''` unsticks typing → 100% confirms modal cleanup leak.

Also worth noting the step before it breaks — e.g. "clicked prompt modal then closed it, then…". That points to the specific overlay.

> DEVELOPER

is there some kind of complexirty there?

> AGENT

Yeah, there's real structural complexity that makes this bug class hard to kill:

**1. ~30 different Base UI `<Dialog>` call sites.** Each one is hand-rolled with its own open-state plumbing. The fix pattern (don't unmount the Dialog while `open=true`, gate children instead) has to be applied correctly in every single file. One slip-up leaks a focus trap. The ESLint rule we added catches the exact `if (!isOpen) return null` above `<Dialog>` pattern, but not variants — e.g. parent doing `{isOpen && <SomeModal />}` has the same effect and the rule doesn't see through the modal wrapper.

**2. Base UI overlays all share the same body-lock mechanism.** Dialog, Select, Popover, Tooltip-with-modal — they all write `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` when open, and rely on their own unmount/close lifecycle to clean up. Any one of them unmounting mid-close leaves the lock. So the leak can come from a Select, a Popover, a Dialog, or an internal Base UI bug — and the user-visible symptom (can't type, Select flashes closed) is identical.

**3. No centralized modal/overlay registry.** There's no single `<ModalProvider>` or portal manager that tracks what's open. Each overlay is its own island. So when something leaks, you can't just look at one place — you have to diagnose in the DOM (the devtools commands I sent).

**4. Nested Tooltip + Button patterns are everywhere.** That `<button> cannot appear as a descendant of <button>` warning you saw earlier is the symptom — `<Tooltip asChild><Button>` wrapping something that also renders a button. Doesn't directly cause the typing bug, but it's the same flavor of "hand-rolled overlay composition" smell.

**5. The focus trap isn't a shared primitive.** Each Base UI overlay manages its own focus scope. If two opened overlays fight over focus (the Select inside a Dialog, or the Dialog that just closed vs the Tooltip that's still open), the tie-breaking is subtle and dependent on mount order and Base UI version.

**What would actually solve this structurally** (not a small task):
- A single `useOverlayStack()` that tracks what's open, and centralizes body pointer-events + focus restore on the *outermost* close, not per-overlay.
- Wrap every Base UI overlay in a thin in-house component that enforces the "let it transition to closed before unmount" invariant.
- Kill `<Tooltip asChild>` → `<Button>` wrapping pattern in favor of a `<TooltipButton>` primitive that doesn't nest buttons.

Short term though, for your current bug, the devtools diagnostic is still the fastest path — it'll tell us which overlay is the leaker and we can fix just that one.

> DEVELOPER

so this could fix the model selector on the edit modal?

> AGENT

Probably yes — but with a caveat.

**If the root cause is a stale focus trap / body-pointer-events leak** (which the symptoms strongly suggest — Select opens and instantly closes = something is pulling focus away), then yes: a centralized overlay stack would fix it by tearing down the body lock only when the *outermost* overlay closes, not per-overlay. No single broken modal could leak state into the next interaction.

**If the cause is something else** — e.g., a parent re-render that changes the Select's `value` or forces it closed via a prop, or the Select's own `onOpenChange` being mis-wired — the structural fix won't help because it's not a leak, it's direct interference.

The devtools diagnostic is worth 60 seconds because it disambiguates these two cases for free:
- `document.body.style.pointerEvents === 'none'` → focus-trap leak → overlay stack fixes it.
- Body clean, but Select still closes → state/prop interference → need to trace the Select's `open` state specifically, fix targeted at this component.

Without that, committing to a multi-day overlay-stack refactor is a gamble. I'd run the 5-line diagnostic first, confirm the cause, then decide whether the fix is "one local patch" or "bigger architectural pass."

Want me to also add a temporary guard that forcibly clears `document.body.style.pointerEvents` whenever the lightbox is interacted with? It's a hack, not a real fix, but it'd unblock you immediately while we figure out the real cause.

> AGENT

Clean. Logs added at 4 choke-points:

1. **`[ModeSelector] click`** — fires when you click Text/Inpaint/Annotate/etc. Shows `activeId`, body pointer-events, open overlays, active element, whether the event was already default-prevented.

2. **`[EditSettings] setEditMode called`** — fires when the persistence setter receives the mode change. Shows previous mode, `hasPersistedSettings`, `isReady`.

3. **`[ModelSelect] trigger click` / `onOpenChange` / `onValueChange`** — the Model dropdown. `onOpenChange` is the smoking-gun log: if it fires with `open: true` then immediately `open: false`, you'll see both events back-to-back with a reason visible in `openOverlays`.

4. **`[PromptTextarea] focus / keydown / onChange / blur`** — textarea. If keydown fires but onChange doesn't, it's being swallowed. If focus doesn't fire when you click it, something is stealing focus.

Reproduce the bug and paste the console output. The pattern will tell us:
- Click mode → ModeSelector log fires but setEditMode doesn't → onClick handler wiring issue.
- Click mode → setEditMode fires but UI doesn't flip → state/re-render issue.
- Model Select trigger click → onOpenChange `true` immediately followed by `false` → focus trap leak (and `openOverlays` at the `false` moment names the culprit).
- Textarea: keydown fires but no onChange → input interception; focus doesn't fire → focus trap.

**Found it.** The Select isn't broken — it's getting *unmounted and remounted* by a re-render storm in a parent.

Look at the log:
- `[ModelSelect] onOpenChange {open: true, bodyPointerEvents: '', openOverlays: Array(0), activeElement: BUTTON}` — Select opens cleanly. **No focus trap, no body lock, no other overlay.**
- Then `[ModelSelect] trigger click`
- Then `open: false` with `activeElement: DIV`
- Then `open: false` again with `activeElement: BODY`

That double-close-with-moving-activeElement is what happens when Base UI's portal tears down — parent re-renders, Select instance changes, onOpenChange(false) fires on teardown.

**The smoking gun is above it**: look at how many times these fire before you even clicked anything:
```
[ModeDebug][GenModeSettings] shotId=… raw generationMode=timeline resolved=timeline
[ModeDebug][EditorController] final generationMode=timeline …
[ModeDebug][ShotSettings] shotId=… status=ready …
[ModeDebug][SettingsProvider] shotId=… status=ready …
```

These fire **dozens of times**. `VideoTravelSettingsProvider.tsx:451` (`GenModeSettings`) is the loudest — it re-renders on every parent render. That provider tree wraps the lightbox, and the re-render storm is remounting components inside it. The Select opens, the parent re-renders, the popover disappears.

Same reason the textarea "can't type" — keystrokes cause state updates → parent re-renders → textarea remounts (or React reconciles with stale props) → input is lost.

**Root cause is not in the lightbox** — it's an unstable context/memo in `VideoTravelSettingsProvider` + `useShotEditorController` + `useShotSettings` rendering on every tick. Let me look:

**Diagnosis**: not a focus trap. A parent re-render storm is unmounting the Select's portal mid-open.

Evidence from your log:
- `bodyPointerEvents: ''` ✅ clean
- `openOverlays: Array(0)` ✅ nothing else open
- `inertCount: 0` ✅ no inert regions

So we can rule out the Phase 1 class of bug entirely.

**The culprit is visible above the click logs**: before you even clicked anything, these fire 30+ times in rapid succession:
```
[ModeDebug][GenModeSettings] shotId=… generationMode=timeline
[ModeDebug][EditorController] final generationMode=timeline
[ModeDebug][ShotSettings] shotId=… status=ready
[ModeDebug][SettingsProvider] shotId=… status=ready
```

Those aren't my logs — they're pre-existing `[ModeDebug]` instrumentation from someone else's debug session in `VideoTravelSettingsProvider.tsx:451` and nearby. They're revealing a real re-render storm in that provider chain. Every time a consumer re-renders, React reconciles the Select's portal, and Base UI fires `onOpenChange(false)` on the teardown — that's your double-close with `activeElement` drifting from `BUTTON` → `DIV` → `BODY`.

Same root cause for your "can't type in textarea" bug: every keystroke → state update → provider re-renders → Select/textarea reconciles from a changing parent → input gets lost.

**Fix direction**: stop the storm in `VideoTravelSettingsProvider` + `useShotSettings` + `useShotEditorController`. Likely culprits:
1. Unstable `handlers` identity (line 286 `providerHandlers` depends on `handlers` from somewhere; if that upstream object recreates every render, everything downstream cascades).
2. `shotSettings.settings` reference churning when values haven't actually changed.
3. An effect in `useShotEditorController` that fires on every render and calls `setState` unconditionally.

Those existing `[ModeDebug]` logs mean someone was already investigating this. Worth asking who put them in — they probably have notes. Want me to dig in and try to find the source, or is this a separate thread you want to tackle outside this session?

> AGENT

Found the root cause. `useShotSettings.ts:85`:
```js
defaults: inheritedSettings || createDefaultVideoTravelSettings(),
```

When `inheritedSettings` is null, `createDefaultVideoTravelSettings()` creates a **brand-new object every render**. That `defaults` reference flows into `useAutoSaveSettings` → `useReactQueryModeLoad`'s effect deps (line 173) → effect re-runs every render → recomputes `loadedSettings = { ...defaults, ...dbSettings }`. Even when deep-equal bails out, there's enough dep churn through the various callbacks (`startLoad`, `applyLoadedData`, `markReady`) to keep triggering recomputations.

Fix — memoize defaults so reference is stable:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/settings/useShotSettings.ts",
  "old_string": "  // Use the shared auto-save hook with inherited settings as initial defaults\n  const autoSave = useAutoSaveSettings<VideoTravelSettings>({\n    toolId: TOOL_IDS.TRAVEL_BETWEEN_IMAGES,\n    shotId,\n    projectId,\n    scope: 'shot',\n    defaults: inheritedSettings || createDefaultVideoTravelSettings(),\n    enabled: !!shotId,\n    debounceMs: 300,\n  });",
  "new_string": "  // Memoize defaults so the reference is stable across renders — an unstable\n  // `defaults` ripples into useAutoSaveSettings' load effects (their deps include\n  // `defaults`), causing the whole settings tree to re-render on every tick.\n  const stableDefaults = useMemo(\n    () => inheritedSettings || createDefaultVideoTravelSettings(),\n    [inheritedSettings],\n  );\n\n  // Use the shared auto-save hook with inherited settings as initial defaults\n  const autoSave = useAutoSaveSettings<VideoTravelSettings>({\n    toolId: TOOL_IDS.TRAVEL_BETWEEN_IMAGES,\n    shotId,\n    projectId,\n    scope: 'shot',\n    defaults: stableDefaults,\n    enabled: !!shotId,\n    debounceMs: 300,\n  });"
}
```
